subject: BRRRR math: the 4 conditions that have to be true (most deals fail at #2)
preheader: Purchase + rehab + holding ≤ 75% ARV · The appraisal risk most investors don't price in

marketSnapshot.headline: BRRRR pencils only when 4 specific conditions hold
marketSnapshot.body: Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat — the BRRRR cycle works powerfully when conditions are aligned and breaks when they're not. The four conditions: (1) Purchase + rehab + holding costs sum to ≤75% of post-rehab ARV. (2) Appraisal supports the ARV (this is where most plans fail). (3) Cash flow positive at refi rates. (4) You can execute the rehab on time and on budget. Miss any one, and capital gets trapped instead of recycled.

dealSpotter.address: Example: BRRRR pencils — all 4 conditions clear
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: All-in $98k vs ARV $145k · refi pulls 75% LTV
dealSpotter.body: $58k purchase + $32k rehab + $8k holding/financing = $98k all-in. Comparable rehabbed properties trading $140-150k. At 75% LTV refi on a $140k appraisal: $105k pulled out (most of your capital recycled), $35k locked in. Cash flow positive at refi rate. The deal works because all four conditions hold — and because the investor used conservative ARV ($140k assumed, $145k hoped-for).

dealSpotter.address: Example: BRRRR marginal — appraisal risk dominates
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Same math, riskier market — appraisals run 5-8% under-comp
dealSpotter.body: Same all-in cost ($98k), same ARV plan ($145k). But the market is one where appraisals consistently come in 5-8% under recent comps. Adjusted ARV = $134k. At 75% LTV refi = $100k pulled out. Only the original capital recycles, no extra capital generated, AND DSCR tightens because the refi loan is smaller. The deal still works on cash flow, but the 'recycle capital and repeat' premise breaks.

$58k purchase + $58k rehab (scope crept) + $12k holding = $128k all-in. ARV $145k. At 75% LTV refi = $108k pulled out. $20k locked in permanently. The rehab over-spend killed the cycle. The lesson: tight rehab scope discipline is the single biggest predictor of whether BRRRR works. Better to do a less-fancy rehab and stay within budget than to over-rehab and trap capital.

qa.question: How do I know if a market is appraisal-friendly or appraisal-hostile for BRRRR?
qa.answer: Pull recent appraisal-vs-sale data from your lender or PM, OR look at the relationship between listing prices and final closing prices in the area. Markets where appraisals consistently match sale prices (final closing within 1-2% of contract price): appraisal-friendly. Markets where 8-15% of deals fall through due to low appraisals or sellers reduce price to match appraisal: appraisal-hostile. Generally appraisal-friendly: stable suburban markets, B-tier neighborhoods with active comparable sales. Generally appraisal-hostile: rapidly gentrifying neighborhoods where rehabbed properties are setting new comps faster than appraisers can absorb, very-low-volume areas where comps are thin, and parts of Detroit/Cleveland/Memphis where the appraisal-vs-sale gap has been 5-10% for years. The practical rule: budget a 5% appraisal haircut on your ARV in unknown markets, and only go below 5% haircut after you have local data.
